newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslav factions condemn attack on Kosovo rector.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslav factions condemn attack on Kosovo rector.

text.p: Several thousand people rallied in Serbia's Albanian-majority province of Kosovo on Saturday to condemn a bomb attack that badly injured the Serb rector of Pristina university, radio Belgrade said.

The major of Pristina told the rally of Serbs and Montenegrins that ethnic Albanian separatists were behind the attack. In Belgrade, the Serbian opposition trying to topple President Slobodan Milosevic said it had nothing to do with the bombing.
Rector Radivoye Papovic was critically wounded on Thursday when a bomb planted in a parked car was exploded as his car passed by, local authorities said.
He was evacuated to a Belgrade hospital for treatment. Private BK television quoted doctors there as saying Papovic would be out of intensive care on Monday.
Kosovo has a 90 percent Albanian majority. The Serbian government revoked its regional autonomy in 1989, accusing the Albanians of wanting to secede and join neighbouring Albania.

"Albanian separatists openly urging Kosovo's secession, acting peace-makers and democrats in front of the international community and supporting opposition protests in Serbia, are behind this most heinous act of political terrorism and ethnic cleansing," Mayor Dusan Simic told the rally Pristina, according to a fax of his comments.
In Belgrade, the Zajedno (Together) opposition coalition released a statement condemning the bomb attack and denying that the Serbian opposition was in any way connected to it.
"Whoever committed this shameless action committed it against the democratisation of Serbia and against the interests of all citizens of Serbia," the Zajedno statement said.
The Orthodox bishop of Rash-Prizren, who ministers to the Orthodox of Kosovo, condemned media reports which he said had prematurely blamed ethnic Albanians for the attack.

"The real culprit should first be found, and this whole event should not be off-handedly linked to parliamentary party of Kosovo leader Adem Demaci," Bishop Artemije said, referring to the ethnic Albanian leader of Kosovo.
